Steam Machines are fundamentally the same as computers. Their operating system is called SteamOS, but it's really a dressed-up version of Linux. It's a good thing—you can launch games, chat with friends etc with only a controller, no keyboard—but you could, if you wanted to, strip down SteamOS into a regular Linux environment. This means that you could run any Linux program on it, like an ordinary Linux desktop (albeit with much more setup).

Lots of companies, like Alienware and Falcon, are making Steam Machines for people to buy. You can, however, just buy a regular computer (or even build one from scratch) and install SteamOS on it. It might not look as slick, but it will work just as well, because Steam Machines are just normal computers running SteamOS.

The one (probable) exception is the Steam Link. It's a really tiny, $50 black box that streams video from your computer to your TV. It doesn't do any of the work required to run the games. Linux might be running the show on them too, but for so little money, it might be custom hardware or something instead.

The different brands of Steam Machines will have different hardware in them. E.g. the Alienware might cost less than the Falcon one, but the latter will perform better (i.e. higher framerates, better graphics). However, by computer standards (and the Steam Machines are computers), they underperform for their price range. The exact specifications are not always given; vague phrases like "Intel® Core processors" and "high performance NVIDIA® GeForce® GTX GPU 2GB GDDR5 graphics" [from Alienware's page] suggest that the parts under the hood aren't all that impressive. The one advantage they share is that they are small, and designed to sit under a TV.

Personally, I would recommend building a desktop computer (a fulfilling and educational experience), and buying a Steam Link if you really, desperately need to play your games on a television. Note that flatscreen TVs usually have longer response times than computer monitors, so in very twitchy, fast-paced games like Super Meat Boy and some competitive shooters, they are not ideal.
